summary: Iteration 5 frontend-only regression + new-feature UI verification on LIVE production Firebase (viewport 390x844). ALL 5 targeted checks PASS. (1) CHECKOUT UI REFACTOR — Online Payment card now shows 'Secure' pill (NOT 'Coming Soon'); button label toggles correctly: COD default => 'Place Order', switch to Online => 'Pay & Place Order', switch back to COD => 'Place Order'. Verified via testIDs pay-cod, pay-online, place-order-btn. (2) COD FULL LIFECYCLE — placed ONE new test order RH74738807 (QA TEST IGNORE, 9999900002, 1x Nutella Hazelnut Spread ₹365 + ₹50 delivery = ₹415, COD). Firestore save logged '[Orders] Firestore order saved successfully: RH74738807'; order-confirmation screen rendered with Status 'Placed', Payment Method 'Cash on Delivery', Invoice INV-RH74738807, discount breakdown Item MRP ₹399 → Product Discount -₹34 → Item Total ₹365 → Delivery Fee ₹50 all present. No regression from checkout.tsx refactor. Full assignment→delivery lifecycle was already exhaustively covered in iteration_4 (RH88275952) and re-verifying end-to-end delivery would require creating another delivery, so this iteration stopped after the confirmation screen per '1 new test order' policy. (3) BULK IMPORT — /admin/products/bulk renders cleanly after admin login; 'Download Excel Template' triggers a real browser download of raha-products-import-template.xlsx (verified via Playwright download event, so Android-safe legacy expo-file-system fallback path is not exercised on web but native code is intact in source). Uploaded a 2-row CSV (test_products.csv): preview shows 2 Rows / 2 Valid / 0 Errors, 'Import 2 Products' CTA enabled, each preview row shows a thumbnail placeholder + an 'Add Image' button (row 1, empty image) and 'Change Image' button (row 2, image URL supplied) — matches spec. Firebase Storage upload was NOT triggered (does not hard-fail per instructions). (4) ORDER SUMMARY DISCOUNT BREAKDOWN — checkout summary card contains Item Total, Delivery Fee, Total Amount rows; confirmation screen shows Item MRP, Product Discount (-₹34), Item Total, Delivery Fee, and admin-side breakdown was already validated in iteration_4. (5) BOTTOM TAB BAR — all 5 tabs (tab-home, tab-categories, tab-cart, tab-orders, tab-profile) visible with readable Ionicons + labels; hidden 'notifications' route is correctly excluded from the bar (href: null branch in CompactTabBar). Height 52px, safe-area padding respected. No red-screen errors anywhere. Deprecated packages detected: none. Pre-existing benign warnings (unchanged since iteration_3/4): shadow* style deprecation from SHADOW tokens, nested <button> hydration warning on product-card, expo-notifications web-listener no-op, props.pointerEvents deprecation, Animated useNativeDriver missing. No new deprecations introduced by this iteration.

critical_code_review_comments: checkout.tsx refactor is clean: finalizeOrder is a single reusable path for both COD and online, with a paymentMeta merge for paid orders. The Object.assign after placeOrder is documented in-file (line 444-449) and is safe because the Firestore write is scheduled on a microtask after the sync return. Confirmed empirically — the created order (RH74738807) was written to Firestore including all decorated fields.

razorpayCheckout.ts native path uses lazy require('react-native-razorpay') — good; web bundles never execute native module and error is not raised on Expo web. RazorpayCancelledError branch differentiated correctly.
payments.ts amount is passed in rupees and rounded on the client — backend still owns the paise conversion + signature secret; no secret leakage to client. Good.

bulk.tsx per-row image upload disables the Import CTA via anyRowUploading useMemo — verified in source (line 626 disabled={... || anyRowUploading}). Could not fully exercise because Firebase Storage upload requires pending Storage rules config per instructions.

(tabs)/_layout.tsx custom CompactTabBar correctly honours the Expo Router hidden-route pattern (href: null branch at line 41-44) so notifications is excluded. Height 52px + insets.bottom padding is Android-safe. Labels use numberOfLines={1} to prevent wrap on narrow devices.
